title: Weekly digest (2 of 4): the dialog that opens when you choose a thing
question: Clicking a thing in the list (or in the preview) opens it in a dialog: its picture (from the media library, for every kind of thing, your #25), the line above the title, title, When and Time on one line, description and registration link, with Cancel bottom left and Save bottom right; Remove from the digest is in the ⋯ at the top. A reworded field has an aqua ring and 'Use the calendar's wording'. Pick the layout. My recommendation: B. It shows the thing as the app and the email will show it while you reword it, so you don't have to save to check how a long title or a picture looks; the dialog is wide, but the page behind is dimmed anyway.

options.label: A: One column of fields
options.thesis: A 640px dialog: the picture across the top with Change picture, then the fields in one column. The preview behind it updates when you save.
options.viewport: Baptisms: picture, Line above the title, Title (reworded), When + Time, Description; Cancel and Save at the foot.
options.risk: You only see how it looks once you've saved and the dialog has closed.

options.label: B: Fields beside how it will look
options.thesis: A wide dialog: the fields on the left; on the right the thing as the app's card and as the email's row, changing as you type.
materials: live app card and email row right
options.viewport: Fields with the reworded title on the left; the Baptisms card and email row with the new title on the right.
options.risk: It covers most of the page, and the two small previews repeat what the big preview shows after saving.

options.label: C: The picture beside the fields
options.thesis: A square picture in a left column with Change picture and Remove, and under it where the thing comes from (calendar, date, place, Open the event); the fields on the right.
options.viewport: Picture and 'From the calendar · Services · Sunday 20 December' on the left, the fields on the right.
options.risk: The square crop isn't how the app (wide) or the email shows the picture.
